The hypothesis only says rho^n is in L^infty, so a negative rho^n would break coercivity. No proof is given.

issues.failure_explanation: The momentum is scaled by {1 - max(0, deltaE/E_kin)}^{1/2}. If deltaE > E_kin (the restart raises potential energy by more than the available kinetic energy), the radicand is negative and the update is undefined. In that case the energy balance cannot be restored by lowering kinetic energy alone. The correct safeguard would cap the ratio (min instead of max), but then the balance is not re-established. The procedure is nevertheless presented as re-establishing discrete energy balance, with no condition guaranteeing deltaE <= E_kin.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Cap the ratio at 1 and state that balance is restored only when deltaE <= E_kin. Optionally give a bound on deltaE from the residual estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The restart-with-relaxation procedure has no guaranteed well-definedness or energy-balance property in the regime deltaE > E_kin.
issues.title: Relaxation restart is ill-defined when the potential-energy gain exceeds the kinetic energy
